subject: Clarify snapshot TTL, offsite backup propagation and EU deletion timeline
messages:
From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@acme-corp.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: EU data delete -> backup propagation question

Hi Soojin,

We have a data subject request coming in for a handful of EU-resident users and Legal has asked for clarity on how deletion requests are propagated into backups. Specifically: 

- When we delete a user record from the live store and request deletion from Redwood, how long until that data is removed from all backup tiers (hot snapshots, warm regional replicas, and cold offsite backups)?
- Does Redwood zero out data immediately or mark tombstones and then sweep?
- If a deletion coincides with an in-flight replication job, is there any window where the data could still be restored?

Can you provide a short timeline and any documentation we can share with our Data Privacy team? We need something to attach to the DSAR response.

Thanks,
Alice
Data Privacy / Acme Corp

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: EU data delete -> backup propagation question

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Summary up front: Redwood treats deletions as logical tombstones immediately and then performs propagation across tiers; full physical purging from all backup layers can take up to 48 hours in typical cases and up to 7 days for rare long-term cold retention windows, unless the record is under legal hold. Below is a concise breakdown you can share with Legal; attaching a retention matrix for reference.

Attachment: backup-retention-matrix.pdf (overview matrix, retention windows by tier)

High-level timeline (EU-resident data):
- T0 (API delete accepted): Redwood marks the record as deleted (tombstone) in the primary cluster within seconds. Logical access is revoked immediately; API reads return 404/erased view.
- T0 -> T0+0-5m: Continuous batching/replication processes pick up tombstone and propagate to regional warm replicas (eu-west-1). For normal traffic this is <5 minutes; under heavy load expect up to ~30 minutes.
- T0 -> T0+0-48h: Backups and offsite snapshots — snapshots taken before T0 may continue to exist until snapshot TTLs expire or are compacted. Our standard snapshot lifecycle (for EU accounts) retains daily snapshots for 14 days by default; automatic snapshot compaction removes unreachable objects within up to 48 hours after tombstone propagation. Cold archival tiers (longer-term retention or customer-managed export) may retain data for longer — see note below.
- Edge cases (very long retention / archival exports): If customer used the optional long-term export/archival feature, deletion from that offsite archive is subject to the archive provider’s purge cycle and can take up to 7 days; Redwood will initiate purge immediately and provide an attest token when completed.

Key behaviors and guarantees:
- Logical deletion (tombstone) = immediate; prevents any new reads.
- Physical purge = background compaction process; typical cascaded purge to all Redwood-managed tiers completed within 48 hours unless long-term archives are in use.
- In-flight replication: If a snapshot started before the tombstone, that snapshot will contain the pre-delete data until that snapshot expires/compacts. We track snapshot genesis timestamps so we can enumerate which snapshots (by id) contain the data.
- Legal hold: If a retention/hold is active at delete time, we will not purge until hold is released; we log hold metadata and provide the Legal team an audit record.

What I need to finalize the DSAR note for Acme:
1) Confirm if you use optional long-term archival export for these users (yes/no).
2) If you need a signed purge attestation when physical purges complete.

Karthik — adding you for any nitty-gritty infra details or if we should call out exact compaction windows / S3 lifecycle configurations for EU tenants.

Adding implementation details to avoid ambiguity:

- Tombstone propagation: Tombstones are emitted into the change-log and applied to regional replicas by the continuous replication worker. Typical observed propagation to eu warm replicas is <5 minutes; 95th percentile on busy days is ~30 minutes.
- Snapshot handling: Our snapshot service creates point-in-time manifests referencing object keys. When a tombstone is applied we mark objects as unreachable; compaction jobs run every 6 hours per region and perform object dereference + physical deletion on objects that are not referenced by any live snapshot. Because compaction is periodic, a pre-delete snapshot may persist until the next compaction run (window up to 6 hours) plus any downstream lifecycle transition (cold archive churn). Combined window: up to ~48 hours end-to-end for typical account configs.
- Offsite cold tiers: We push exports to the customer-configured cold bucket (if enabled) asynchronously. If Acme has that feature enabled, deletion from the cold bucket requires both Redwood purge request and downstream provider lifecycle; we typically see provider-side purge complete within 3–7 days.
- Restore/restore-certificates: We log snapshot ids and object manifests. If you request a restore before compaction finishes, support can enumerate the snapshot ids and confirm whether the deleted record would be included. We do not automatically restore deleted records once tombstoned; restores are always an explicit operation and require the account owner's auth.

Operational notes for Legal evidence:
- We can provide a snapshot id list, compaction logs, and an audit record for the purge job.
- For EU accounts we keep audit logs in-region; we can deliver a signed attestation when physical purge completes (this is the standard for enterprise DSAR responses).

I attached a small diagram of the replication flow for reference.

Attachments: s3-replication-architecture.png

Alice — thanks for the patience. Per Karthik’s note, I’ve summarized a DSAR-friendly paragraph you can paste into the vendor response and I included the two attachments (retention matrix + replication diagram).

Suggested DSAR language (short):
"Upon a deletion request Redwood immediately marks the subject data as deleted (logical tombstone) and revokes API access. Tombstone propagation to in-region replicas occurs within minutes; subsequent snapshot compaction and background purge processes remove references from Redwood-managed snapshots and backups. For standard EU account configurations, full physical removal from Redwood-managed tiers completes within 48 hours in most cases. If the data was exported to customer-configured cold archives, Redwood initiates a purge immediately and the downstream provider may require up to 7 days to complete physical removal. All deletion and purge actions are logged, and Redwood can provide signed attestations and the relevant audit records on request. Legal holds will prevent purges until lifted."

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether Acme uses the optional cold-archive export so we can call out the longer window if needed.
- If you want an attestation, reply YES and include the preferred contact for signature.

If Legal needs anything more formal (wording changes, additional log extracts), loop me and Marissa and we’ll queue a support ticket to generate the artifacts.
